title: Side-level versus patient-level evaluation in four-view mammography classification: a comprehensive benchmark on the CMMD dataset

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Side-level versus patient-level evaluation in four-view mammography classification: a comprehensive benchmark on the CMMD dataset》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · abstract-1-1】Deep learning for mammographic image classification yields impressive performance metrics, but inconsistent evaluation methodologies-specifically whether results are reported at the independent side level or the bilateral patient level-make cross-study comparisons unreliable. The aim of this study was to quantify, on a single dataset and with a uniform training recipe, how much of the reported performance is determined by evaluation granularity rather than by model architecture.

【Introduction · S0002-p1】Computer-aided detection and diagnosis (CAD) systems for the analysis of mammographic images have advanced rapidly with the adoption of deep learning [1,2]. Recent studies report area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.95 for malignancy detection, sometimes approaching or surpassing expert radiologists. However, these impressive numbers often obscure fundamental inconsistencies in how performance is measured and reported. Beyond reporting consistency, recent reviews have identified broader implementation challenges—reproducibility, evidentiary standards, technological maturity, user trust, and ethical and legal frameworks—that must be resolved before AI is safely adopted in breast cancer screening programs [3].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Side-level versus patient-level evaluation in four-view mammography classification: a comprehensive benchmark on the CMMD dataset》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Evaluation methodology in medical imaging · S0003-S2003-p1】The importance of consistent evaluation in medical imaging has been highlighted by several meta-analyses [12,13]. However, specific analysis of how evaluation granularity (side-level vs. patient-level) affects reported performance in mammography has received limited attention. This gap motivates the systematic benchmark presented in this work.

【Methodology · S0004-p1】An overview of the full evaluation pipeline—from raw four-view inputs through preprocessing, fold assignment, the shared backbone, the three fusion strategies, the dual-head classifier, and the side-level and patient-level metrics—is shown in Figure 1. Each stage is described in detail in the corresponding subsection below.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Side-level versus patient-level evaluation in four-view mammography classification: a comprehensive benchmark on the CMMD dataset》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Summary of findings · S0007-S2001-p1】The most consequential finding is that evaluation methodology matters more than model choice on this dataset. Side-level AUC exceeds patient-level AUC by 17.5% on average—a gap that dwarfs all architectural differences among CNNs (<3%) and represents the single largest source of variability in our benchmark, yet it reflects a reporting choice rather than a model property.

【Summary of findings · S0007-S2001-p2】At the architectural level, absolute CNN-vs-CNN AUC differences are small (≤0.030 on pooled per-case scores; the conservative 5-fold Wilcoxon test resolves none of them, while higher-power DeLong paired tests resolve approximately half), and the top five CNNs fall within 0.7% AUC of each other at side level. Meanwhile, ViT-B/16 substantially underperforms all CNN variants by approximately 9% AUC, consistent with the established observation that vision transformers require larger training sets than are typically available in medical imaging. The per-case analysis further reveals that ViT fails on a partially different patient population than CNNs (Jaccard overlap 0.29 vs. 0.42 for CNN-CNN pairs), suggesting architectural complementarity despite inferior individual performance.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Side-level versus patient-level evaluation in four-view mammography classification: a comprehensive benchmark on the CMMD dataset》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Overview of the evaluation pipeline. Inputs (blue) flow through preprocessing and fold assignment (orange), the shared backbone, one of three fusion strategies, and the shared dual-head classifier; outputs are summarized at both the side and patient level (green). All four views of a patient share a fold by construction.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Side-level AUC vs. patient-level AUC for all configurations (diagnosis task). All points fall well below the y=x line, demonstrating systematic inflation of side-level metrics. Error bars show ±1 std across 5 folds.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Side-level (left) and patient-level (right) AUC by backbone and fusion strategy for binary diagnosis. CNN backbones cluster tightly at side level; patient-level reveals greater variance.

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《Side-level versus patient-level evaluation in four-view mammography classification: a comprehensive benchmark on the CMMD dataset》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Data availability statement · S0010-p1】The CMMD dataset is publicly available through The Cancer Imaging Archive. The complete benchmark code (benchmark_mammography.py), the post-hoc reanalysis script used in this revision (bootstrap_and_delong.py), and the per-fold and per-case predictions for all 16 configurations on both tasks are publicly available at https://github.com/Minds-R-Lab/side-vs-patient-mammography under the MIT license, with a README documenting how to reproduce every table, figure, and statistical test in this manuscript. A Zenodo DOI for archival citation will be minted prior to camera-ready publication.
